## Trial `cron-access-control-ubuntu24__omZ9ZSc`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin using /etc/cron.allow, created the missing opsadmin account, and directly proved both allow and deny behavior for multiple users before and after a full, evidenced node restart. The restart evidence protocol (pre-restart boot id/baseline, reboot acknowledgement, disconnection, reconnection with a new boot id, and full post-restart re-verification of config/service/enforcement) is complete and corroborated by the independent lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is slightly reduced by an apparently unintended extra test-user creation (testuser2) caused by a shell redirection quirk, but it was fully cleaned up and left no residue.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.950 | 11/2 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cron-allow-restricted — Satisfied:** On node1, only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (create/install crontabs)
  - **Why:** /etc/cron.allow was created containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', with no /etc/cron.deny present, which under Vixie cron's allow-list semantics restricts crontab usage to only the listed users. This is directly observed both pre- and post-restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c0b91ab54890478f`, `cmd-d5b79c3545fb45b4`, `cmd-bafbdddf2666464b`
- **opsadmin-exists-and-allowed — Satisfied:** opsadmin user exists and can schedule cron jobs
  - **Why:** opsadmin did not exist on the node; executor created it (uid 1000) and directly demonstrated it can install and list a crontab, both before and after restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-edc6f35a72474fe2`, `cmd-19675c1c304949bf`, `cmd-bafbdddf2666464b`
- **root-allowed — Satisfied:** root can schedule cron jobs
  - **Why:** root successfully installed and listed a crontab entry before and after restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-19675c1c304949bf`, `cmd-bafbdddf2666464b`
- **other-users-denied — Satisfied:** Users other than root and opsadmin are denied cron scheduling
  - **Why:** A freshly created non-listed user (testdeny) and a pre-existing system account (nobody) were both directly shown to be denied with 'cannot use this program (crontab)', both pre- and post-restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-56224bd3de70430d`, `cmd-bafbdddf2666464b`
- **restart-persistence — Satisfied:** Cron access restriction and enforcement persist across a full node restart (independent restart-evidence protocol)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (bdd5de93...) and healthy cron.allow/service state were captured, a reboot was acknowledged and executed, boot_id changed post-restart (ec37444a...) confirming an actual reboot, and cron.allow contents, cron service status, opsadmin user, and allow/deny enforcement were all re-verified identical to pre-restart state. The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the same boot_id transition and show no failed services or package-health issues after the restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8b36656a893046f9`, `cmd-20a70bcf2e794004`, `cmd-a57357a09ea44829`, `cmd-be89889a222843fd`, `cmd-bec7e9eca0094926`, `cmd-bafbdddf2666464b`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor commands were mostly narrowly scoped: useradd for opsadmin (required), cron.allow creation (required), temporary test users (testdeny, and an apparently-unintended testuser2 created via a shell-redirection quirk in cmd-56224bd3de70430d: 'useradd ... testuser2>/dev/null' parses as creating user testuser2 with stdout redirected, not as a no-op), test crontab entries, and a controlled reboot. All test artifacts (test crontabs, testdeny, testuser2) were fully removed in cmd-92c28f5290324033 and cmd-54d4445e67cb4791, and the fixed after_executor snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected persistent temp files, and healthy package state. The one unnecessary mutation (creation of testuser2, likely an unintended side effect of a shell quoting mistake rather than a deliberate test) was bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted, so it only modestly reduces the hygiene score.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-56224bd3de70430d`, `cmd-92c28f5290324033`, `cmd-54d4445e67cb4791`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`
